key_insight: Onnes couples a physics-based dilution-refrigerator digital twin with a multi-agent LLM layer to diagnose cryogenic faults, and can match a supervised classifier when given a few contrastive demonstrations plus self-consistency voting.
engineering_relevance: This matters for quantum hardware operations because it moves cryostat monitoring from simple threshold alarms to interpretable fault identification with sim-to-real potential.
method: Forward physics model of a dilution refrigerator plus learned noise/correlation fingerprint from real BlueFors logs
Six physics-grounded fault classes, including overlapping-temperature cases separated by flow and pressure
Zero-shot multi-agent LLM panel, then few-shot contrastive demonstrations and self-consistency voting for improved classification
evidence_signal: In a 1000-turn evaluation, classification improved from 0.685 to 0.990 with six labeled demonstrations, matching a supervised classifier at 0.985; a real-hardware detector showed 6.4% false alarms and 100% recall on injected faults.
watch_item: Performance and false-alarm behavior depend on the backend and confidence gating, so deployment will need careful calibration before use in live cryogenic operations.
paper_title: Onnes: A Physics-Grounded Multi-Agent LLM Simulator for Cryogenic Fault Diagnosis in Quantum Computing Infrastructure
